title: Machine learning separates hemorrhagic from ischemic stroke using clinical variables
summary: An XGBoost model using clinical variables in 2,418 development patients reached an internal AUROC of 0.937, and in an independent external cohort of 580 patients from a third center the AUROC was 0.841. SHAP values were used to assess feature contributions. The study is retrospective and the model is decision support, not a replacement for neuroimaging.
ai_technology: XGBoost model with SHAP feature attribution
organization: Chungbuk National University; Chungbuk National University Hospital

evidence.tested: Four-fold internal validation and independent external validation at a third stroke center.
evidence.unknown: Prospective emergency-department performance and effect on care; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A gradient-boosted model distinguished stroke subtype from presentation variables.
